newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ sees 'measurable' computer bug cost.
newsitem.headline: ANZ sees 'measurable' computer bug cost.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) said on Wednesday it expected the cost of fixing the computer "millenium bug" would result in a sizeable cost.
"The cost of the millenium programme will not be large. But it would be measurable," ANZ's outgoing chief executive officer Don Mercer told reporters.
"We feel we understand our situation pretty well and we expect to have that dealt with quite satisfactory by the end of 1998," Mercer said.
The millenium bug is a worldwide programming problem that will cause computers to view the year 2000 as the year 1900.
The millenium bug will occur as a result of a programming fault which only allows computers to accept the last two digits of a year.
As a result, companies will have to re-programme their computers to accept a four-digit field before 2000 in order to avoid computer chaos.
ANZ earlier reported an 18 percent rise in first half net profit to A$615 million and lifted its interim dividend to 22 cents per share from 18 cents a year ago.
